title: Chris Justice (Engenious Design) — 'If your organization's metrics don't fight each other, they aren't that good'
summary: Chris Justice — leader at Engenious Design (engineering firm) — reads Incorruptible and lands on the airline example (lowest cost + highest employee satisfaction + highest customer satisfaction + highest profits): if the metrics don't fight each other, they're too simple to accurately reflect reality. Applies it to how his own team measures itself.
blockquote: If your organization's metrics don't fight each other, they aren't that good. Because that means they are too simple to accurately reflect reality. This is one takeaway as I read Eric Ries book 'Incorruptible'. He cites the example of an airline that had these goals: Lowest cost, Highest employee satisfaction, Highest customer satisfaction, Highest profits.
